notes: §1985:IX.4.4.2 prints OPEN followed by a repeatable choice of INPUT, OUTPUT, I-O or EXTEND, each with one or more file-names, and no other phrase (the indexed format has neither REVERSED nor NO REWIND). openStatement is OPEN openClause+ and openClause is openMode then openFileSpec+, so every mode may repeat and each takes a list of names; BindOpen binds one BoundOpenFile per file-name in source order for every edition (§1985:IX.4.4.4 GR17: "the same as if a separate OPEN statement had been written for each file-name"), with no edition arm needed for the 1985 shape. What the superset grammar adds is refused at --std 85: the SHARING phrase by VisitOpenStatement and the RETRY phrase by VisitRetryPhrase (both COBOL0900), and a REVERSED or WITH NO REWIND written after an indexed file-name by CheckOpenTapePhrase (COBOL2210, COBOL1802: the OpenTapePhraseRule rows admit sequential organization only); a mode with no file-name and a file-name with no mode are syntax errors. Probed at 85: OPEN OUTPUT F1 F2, OPEN INPUT F1 I-O F2, OPEN EXTEND F1 INPUT F2 and OPEN INPUT F1 INPUT F2 on indexed files compile and run with status 00; OPEN INPUT F REVERSED, WITH NO REWIND, SHARING WITH ALL OTHER and RETRY 3 TIMES are each refused. The witness opens one indexed file OUTPUT, INPUT and I-O in turn and displays status 00.

next.reason: 1985 indexed OPEN: OPEN {INPUT|OUTPUT|I-O|EXTEND} {file-name} …, repeated. §2023:14.9.27.2 keeps the four repeatable modes and adds [ sharing-phrase ] [ retry-phrase ] and WITH NO REWIND; for an indexed file §2023:14.9.27.3 SR5 still refuses NO REWIND ("The NO REWIND phrase may be specified only for sequential files"), so the added indexed cases are the sharing and retry phrases (e.g. OPEN INPUT SHARING WITH READ ONLY idx-file), accepted at compile time. 1985 OPEN statements keep their meaning; no refusal became an exception.
